scope: Frozen upstream source FIFO, trusted frame publication, transport protected slot/retry pipeline. Actual BLE owner implementation intentionally excluded while being edited. No hardware access; production source unchanged by reviewer.

findings.problem: The lifecycle and newly queued protected descriptors are always selected before the owned protected retry. A sustained lifecycle backlog prevents expiry processing indefinitely, so the advertised total one-second protected transaction deadline does not bound owned-slot retirement even though the transport task keeps running.
findings.actualReproducer: One protected NO_MEM retry; fifty lifecycle records selected at100ms intervals. After5s the original1s deadline has expired but retainedOwner=1 and expiryCount=0. Once lifecycle backlog stops the next iteration releases it.
findings.recommendation: Perform bounded expiration housekeeping independently of higher-priority send selection. Only release a descriptor already owned by this transport task or explicitly removed from its queue. Do not claim SDK cancellation, reclaim BLE-owned slots, or demote critical send priority.

ownershipReview: Actual acquisition publication has one producer: main acquisition owner calls AsyncLogPublishFrameSnapshot. AsyncLogTask is the sole scientific NetFramePublish/TransportPublishFrame caller.

Source FIFO removal and marking state3 OWNED occur under the same s_asyncLogMux. Supersession only scans/removes that protected pending ring under the same mux; WRITING/OWNED slots are not candidates.

Transport supersession does not scan a potentially stale PENDING slot flag. It must first acquire a descriptor with xQueueReceive; a descriptor already removed by the consumer cannot be reclaimed by that producer. Owned retry is exclusively transport-task state outside the queue.
Payload/frame/typed identity copies occur after reservation and before publishing to the consumer; consumer copies are outside short critical sections with exclusive slot ownership.

Ordinary capacity remains four source slots/four transport shared normal slots. Two source and two transport protection reservations are additional separate capacity; one lifecycle transport slot remains reserved.
Failed real encoding frees only its reserved source slot and retains the candidate obligation; new missed-first counters do not label the original candidate as delivered.

Synchronous BLE publication receives both original full payload and optional normal SHORT preview. The protected full identity comes from the encoder-paired frame, not ParseFrameMeta or current global configuration.
orderingReview: Source output is one FIFO, including protected reservations, so formal USB publication order does not become protected-first. Pending supersession is counted omission, not relabeling.

Transport selects protected frames before ordinary frames; BLE obsolete fence drops older/equal sequence only within the same session/boot and captured connection. Cross-boot identities are never numerically ordered.

Wi-Fi retains each descriptor original bytes/identity even when BLE skips/obsoletes it. Its send order can now be protected-before-older-ordinary. No reviewed contract promises UDP/parallel-transport in-order delivery; document the local scheduling change rather than discarding Wi-Fi frames based on BLE admission.
USB publication order is not a claim of host receipt or order on another transport.
initializationReview: Source six-slot allocation uses existing ensure helper, prefers PSRAM, retains successful workspace on second-pool allocation failure, and returnsNO_MEM before any producer can become running.
Successful/live task storage cannot be reset by later Init: already-started returnsOK; a nonnull task handle before started publication returnsINVALID_STATE.
Transport protected queue/pool are static. Init rejects missing handles; no runtime full-payload allocation is introduced.
